column1: # family|takeaway|original cue|retry cue|review cue

qb1-d01|Separate routine measurement from nursing interpretation and evaluation.|The RN has assessed a stable client and established the plan.|The intake/output plan is established for a stable client.|The new weight trend needs interpretation.

qb1-d02|Reassess delegation when the client's circumstances change.|The comparison asks which client has stable glucose readings.|New dizziness appeared before the planned walk.|The client is asymptomatic with stable readings and reporting instructions.

qb1-d03|Do not delay RN assessment of an unexpected concerning finding.|BP has newly fallen from 124/78 to 88/52.|A previously afebrile postoperative client now has a temperature of 39.2°C.|The RN postponed assessing newly low BP.

qb1-d04|Match LPN assignments to the stated scope, competence, and established care plan.|The client is stable and the assignment must be authorized for the LPN.|Local rules allow reinforcing education already planned by the RN.|Independent comprehensive planning is reserved to the RN in this setting.

qb1-d05|Delegation includes follow-up and RN evaluation of the client's response.|The RN delegated an established walk for a stable client.|The UAP reports completing the planned walk.|New pain occurs during a walk with stop-and-report instructions.

qb1-d06|Both role authorization and procedure-specific competence are needed.|The setting authorizes the dressing change for a competent LPN, not the UAP.|Policy reserves this procedure to a licensed nurse.|The LPN has not demonstrated competence in this procedure.

qb1-d07|The RN remains accountable for the delegation decision; each person remains accountable for their own actions.|The question asks specifically about the delegation decision.|The task is permitted and the UAP is competent.|A complication occurred, but the circumstances still need review.

qb1-i01|During donning, extend gloves over the gown cuffs.|The student asks why gloves follow the gown.|Wrist skin is exposed between the gloves and sleeves.|The glove openings leave a gap below the gown cuffs.

qb1-i02|Use the specified PPE removal method; CDC describes more than one method.|This question specifies separate PPE removal.|CDC Example 1 is specified, and gloves have been removed.|The nurse is using CDC Example 2 with gown and gloves together.

qb1-i03|Clean hands after PPE removal and promptly if contamination occurs during removal.|PPE has just been removed in the appropriate location.|A bare hand becomes contaminated during removal.|PPE removal is complete and the nurse is about to use shared equipment.

qb1-i04|Standard precautions continue for every client; select measures based on exposure risk.|The question concerns the baseline precautions for all clients.|No symptoms and a negative screen do not remove the need for standard precautions.|Transmission-based precautions have been added.

qb1-i05|Remove a used surgical mask by its ties or loops without touching the front.|The nurse is removing a used surgical mask.|CDC Example 1's preceding removal steps have been completed.|The question asks which mask surface to avoid touching.

qb1-i06|Avoid transferring contamination to the face or a clean site; change gloves and clean hands when indicated.|The nurse is working while wearing PPE.|Soiled-linen handling is followed by an aseptic task.|Contaminated gloves must not be used to adjust the mask.

qb1-i07|Handle used eye protection by its headband or ear pieces and send reusable items for reprocessing.|CDC Example 1 and used goggles are specified.|Reusable eye protection is being removed.|Correctly removed goggles still need reprocessing before reuse.

qb1-p01|Recognize postoperative stridor as an urgent airway warning in these scenarios.|Stridor follows thyroidectomy.|New stridor follows neck surgery.|The comparison is stridor versus expected pain with stable findings.

qb1-p02|Prioritize the new concerning change over an unchanged stable baseline in the stated comparison.|One client's abdominal pain is new and worsening; the other's pain is unchanged.|Chronic arthritis does not explain away new severe abdominal pain.|The abdominal pain is worsening, unlike the stable baseline arthritis pain.

qb1-p03|Active significant bleeding and associated symptoms warrant urgent assessment and escalation.|Blood is rapidly soaking a surgical dressing.|Rapidly expanding bloody drainage occurs with dizziness.|Fresh bleeding and lightheadedness compete with routine teaching.

qb1-p04|Interpret concerning vital signs together with the client's symptoms and trend.|The postoperative client is hypotensive, tachycardic, pale, and restless.|Low BP, fast pulse, and restlessness are new.|Pallor and restlessness accompany new hypotension.

qb1-p05|Promptly assess a new mental-status change instead of accepting it as baseline.|The client was alert and oriented this morning but is now confused.|Disorientation appeared within an hour.|The confusion is new in a previously oriented client.

qb1-p06|A falling oxygen saturation with new breathlessness needs prompt attention over routine requests.|Saturation fell from 96% to 88% with new shortness of breath.|Saturation fell from 97% to 88% with new dyspnea.|New breathlessness accompanies a falling saturation.

qb2-f01|Compare active ingredients to avoid duplicate acetaminophen products.|Both OTC products contain acetaminophen.|Different brand names conceal the same active ingredient.|Spacing duplicate products by an hour does not prevent their doses from adding together.

qb2-f02|Keep vitamin K intake consistent during warfarin treatment and discuss major changes.|The client takes warfarin and asks about leafy vegetables.|A major increase in leafy vegetables is planned.|The statement proposes eliminating vitamin K foods completely.

qb2-f03|Separate the specified levothyroxine tablet and calcium by at least four hours.|Levothyroxine is scheduled at 6 a.m.|Levothyroxine is scheduled at 7 a.m.|Calcium is being taken only one hour later.

qb2-f04|Follow the FOSAMAX tablet's water, fasting, and upright instructions.|The client can swallow and remain upright.|The client plans to lie down immediately after the tablet.|The proposed dose is taken with breakfast and coffee.

qb2-f05|Do not cut, crush, or chew the specified metformin ER tablet; seek a suitable alternative.|This product's label explicitly prohibits modification.|The proposed half-tablet conflicts with this label.|The client cannot swallow the whole tablet.

qb2-f06|For the verified splittable metoprolol ER product, swallow the prescribed portion without crushing or chewing.|The pharmacist verified that this exact scored product can be divided.|Splitting was permitted, but crushing and chewing were not.|Different ER products can have different splitting instructions.

qb2-f07|For CIPRO and the specified antacid, distinguish two hours before from six hours after.|The antacid contains magnesium and aluminum.|CIPRO is scheduled before the antacid.|The antacid was taken at noon and CIPRO will follow it.

qb2-f08|Follow the stated ELIQUIS missed-dose directions without doubling a dose.|The client asks about standard missed-dose instructions without bleeding or an interruption order.|The scenario concerns a missed ELIQUIS dose.|Doubling is not the labeled way to make up a missed ELIQUIS dose.
qb2-f09|Do not mix the specified LANTUS insulin with another insulin.|LANTUS U-100 is the specified insulin.|Mixing is proposed for LANTUS.|The product identity determines the mixing restriction.

qb2-f10|An insulin pen is for one patient, even when a new needle is used.|The question concerns sharing an insulin pen.|Changing the needle does not make pen sharing safe.|A previously used pen differs from unused packaged supplies.

qb2-f11|Keep NITROSTAT in its original glass container with the cap tightly closed.|The client asks about NITROSTAT storage.|The tablets were transferred into a plastic weekly box.|The original container has just been opened for a dose.

qb2-f12|Antibiotics do not treat an uncomplicated viral cold.|The clinician diagnosed a viral cold without bacterial infection.|Mucus color changed, but the stated diagnosis remains viral.|The proposed antibiotic is not needed for the confirmed viral cause.

qb2-f13|Avoid alcohol during opioid treatment because the combination can dangerously depress breathing and alertness.|The client newly prescribed an opioid asks about alcohol.|A two-hour gap is proposed as protection.|The client assumes taking alcohol with dinner makes the combination safe.

qb2-f14|Measure an oral liquid with a suitable medication device marked in the prescribed units.|The dose is written in mL.|Only an unmarked kitchen spoon is available.|The caregiver is estimating a dose with a household teaspoon.
qb2-f15|Include OTC medicines and supplements in a current medication list.|The client omitted OTC products and supplements.|The herbal product is used intermittently.|A prescription dose changed.

qb2-f16|Verify splitting instructions for the exact tablet product.|The manufacturer changed even though medicine and strength stayed the same.|A replacement product may have different splitting instructions.|A score line alone is being treated as sufficient verification.

qb2-f17|Follow the current prescribed antibiotic plan and seek advice before changing it yourself.|Symptoms improved without adverse effects or a revised order.|The prescriber issued a revised plan.|The client feels better but has no revised instructions.

qb2-f18|Do not rely on appearance or an intact seal to justify using an expired medicine.|The expired medicine looks unchanged and the symptom is nonurgent.|Correct storage and normal appearance do not extend the date.|The unopened product is past its printed expiration date.

qb2-f19|Use the active-ingredient section to identify duplicate OTC medicines and amounts.|The client wants to compare ingredients and amounts.|The question asks for ingredient amount per dosage unit.|Different advertised uses may still involve the same ingredient.

qb2-f20|Use an available authorized take-back option; follow product-specific disposal guidance when it is unavailable.|An accepting authorized take-back location is readily accessible.|An authorized mail-back option is available.|No take-back option is readily available and the medicine is on the FDA flush list.

qb3-g01|Use teach-back to check understanding and adjust the explanation when needed.|The nurse needs to check understanding of a home plan.|The client's explanation reveals confusion.|Reading the words aloud does not show how the client will apply them.

qb3-g02|Offer evidence-supported help for quitting rather than treating medication or counseling as failure.|The adult wants help quitting cigarettes.|The client cannot travel for coaching.|The client views needing medication as failure.

qb3-g03|Distinguish mild illness from a more substantial acute illness during vaccine screening.|The adult has only a mild cold and no identified vaccine-specific contraindication.|Screening identifies moderate acute illness.|The statement treats any runny nose as an automatic prohibition.

qb3-g04|Use consistent positioning, rest, and appropriate cuff fit for home BP measurements.|Seated BP measurement positioning is the issue.|The client has just hurried upstairs.|Cuff sizes and measurement positions differ.

qb3-g05|Communicate respectfully with simple wording and enough time to respond.|The client with established dementia needs extra response time.|An open-ended beverage question is difficult for the client.|The client has not understood the instruction.

qb3-g06|Invite discussion of the concern without promising that a procedure has no risk.|The stable client is anxious about tomorrow's procedure.|The client is worried about recovery.|The response promises there are no risks.

qb3-g07|Listen and offer support without imposing one way or timeline for grieving.|The bereaved adult wants to talk about their spouse.|The person asks about support beyond family.|Two people respond differently to similar losses.

qb3-g08|Acknowledge distress without affirming a hallucination, while addressing safety concerns.|Immediate safety concerns have been assessed and the voices are frightening.|The care plan addresses recurring hallucinations without a new safety concern.|The client asks whether the nurse shares the perception.

qb3-g09|Avoid vigorous rubbing or massage of vulnerable skin in pressure-injury prevention.|The client has vulnerable sacral skin.|A caregiver proposes rubbing reddened skin.|The proposed instruction is vigorous massage over bony areas.

qb3-g10|Keep catheter drainage dependent and unobstructed, with the bag off the floor.|The question concerns drainage-bag position.|The bag was placed on the abdomen during transfer.|The tubing is kinked beneath a bedrail.

qb3-g11|Choose dry-mouth comfort measures consistent with swallowing safety and the fluid plan.|The adult can swallow safely and has no fluid restriction.|A prescribed fluid limit must be considered.|The adult can swallow safely and asks about sugarless gum.

qb3-g12|Support sleep with a suitable environment and consistent routines.|The question concerns the home sleep environment.|Late screen use precedes difficulty settling.|The proposed plan concerns bed and wake times.

qb3-g13|Act on peripheral-IV phlebitis signs even if the infusion still flows.|A nonvesicant IV is warm, red, and tender along the vein.|Tenderness and redness are new despite continued flow.|Phlebitis is present at a nonvesicant peripheral IV.

qb3-g14|Possible GI bleeding warrants prompt evaluation rather than automatic reassurance.|New black tarry stool occurs with lightheadedness.|The vomit resembles coffee grounds.|Black tarry stool is accompanied by dizziness.

qb3-g15|Escalate sudden postoperative breathlessness and chest pain urgently.|Symptoms begin suddenly at home after surgery.|Sudden dyspnea occurs even without leg swelling.|Chest pain accompanies unexplained breathlessness after surgery.

qb3-g16|Clarify and reconcile a newly reported drug reaction before routine administration.|The client reports a past reaction absent from the record.|The question asks which reaction details are useful.|The chart and the client's report of hives conflict.

qb3-g17|Treat sudden stroke-like symptoms as an emergency, including when symptoms improve.|Facial droop and slurred speech begin suddenly.|One-sided weakness improves before help arrives.|Onset and last-known-well information may differ.

qb3-g18|Use oral fast-acting carbohydrate only when the person can swallow safely and the stated protocol applies.|The adult is alert, can swallow, and has glucose 64 mg/dL under a 15-15 order.|Glucose remains 66 mg/dL at the protocol's 15-minute recheck.|The question asks which adult can safely receive oral treatment.

qb3-g19|Severe asthma symptoms unrelieved by prescribed treatment require emergency help.|Severe breathing difficulty continues despite reliever treatment.|Breathing remains very hard after reliever use.|The severe attack has not responded to the client's medicines.

qb3-g20|Compare daily heart-failure weights under consistent conditions and follow the reporting plan.|The question concerns the daily weighing routine.|Today's measurement follows breakfast and adds a heavy robe.|Morning and evening readings were taken in different clothing.
